name: Planning a Full Kitchen Overhaul: Timeline and Phase Guide

step.name: Step 1: Planning, design documentation, and municipal permitting
step.text: Your contractor surveys existing wall studs, measures plumbing stacks, and draws architectural layouts. Once you approve appliance models and cabinet designs, your team submits plans to the local building department for review, which can take anywhere from a few days for basic work to several weeks for structural wall removals.

step.name: Step 2: Site protection and complete demolition down to framing
step.text: Crews seal off adjacent living spaces using heavy plastic barriers and floor protection to control dust. The kitchen is stripped bare, removing old cabinetry, worn countertops, damaged subflooring, and targeted drywall to reveal the framing beneath.

step.name: Step 3: Rough mechanical rough-ins and structural framing changes
step.text: Carpenters frame any new wall openings or island supports while licensed trade partners install rough plumbing drains, gas lines, ventilation ducts, and new electrical circuits. Rough municipal inspections take place during this window before any insulation or wallboard can go up.

step.name: Step 4: Drywall installation, taping, and background finish prep
step.text: Workers hang water-resistant drywall, apply tape, coat seams, and sand the surfaces smooth. A prime coat of paint and level floor prep are completed during this phase so finish surfaces sit on an even foundation.

step.name: Step 5: Cabinet installation, trim carpentry, and countertop templating
step.text: Installers anchor base and upper cabinets level against wall studs. Precise stone fabricators template the countertops, while finish carpenters install crown molding, baseboards, and decorative trim details.

step.name: Step 6: Tile backsplash, fixture trim-out, and final municipal inspection
step.text: Crews lay tile and marble backsplashes, connect sink plumbing, and hook up appliances. The city inspector conducts the final inspection, and your contractor completes a final walkthrough with you. Ready to plan your kitchen remodel in the Denver area?
